                "Part": 1,
                "Section": "B",
                "SectionName": "Planning, Budgeting, and Forecasting",
                "Topic": "B.037 flexible budget variance interpretation",
                "MicroTopic": "flexible budget variance interpretation",
                "UniqueConceptKey": "B-037-flexible-budget-variance-interpretation",
                "LOSTag": "B.4 Annual profit plan and supporting schedules",
                "Difficulty": "Moderate",
                "ItemType": "MCQ",
                "ItemStyle": "single-select",
                "Stem": "Delta's flexible budget for 8,000 units shows budgeted variable costs of $64,000. Actual output was 8,000 units with actual variable costs of $70,000. What does this variance indicate?",
                "Choices": {
                        "A": "An unfavorable spending variance of $6,000 since output matched the flex budget",
                        "B": "A favorable volume variance of $6,000",
                        "C": "An unfavorable efficiency variance caused by higher production volume",
                        "D": "No variance exists because actual output equals budgeted output"
                },
                "CorrectChoice": "A",
                "ExplanationCorrect": "Since actual output (8,000 units) matches the flexed budget level, any difference between actual and flexed budgeted costs is a spending variance, not a volume variance. $70,000 - $64,000 = $6,000 unfavorable spending variance.",
                "StudyLinks": [
                        {
                                "label": "IMA CMA Learning Outcome Statements, Part 1 Section B",
                                "url": "https://prodcm.imanet.org/-/media/IMA/Files/Home/IMA-Certifications/CMA-Certification/2024-CMA-Learning-Outcome-Statement-Final.ashx"
                        },
                        {
                                "label": "OpenStax Managerial Accounting: Budgeting",
                                "url": "https://openstax.org/books/principles-managerial-accounting/pages/7-introduction"
                        }
                ],
                "SourceDescription": "Original CMA Part 1 exam-style practice. Not real CMA exam content and not copied from official samples.",
                "Part1OnlyFlag": true,
                "ReviewNote": "If missed or marked, review the linked study materials and rework the underlying concept without looking at the answer.",
                "QuestionID": "P1-B-037",
                "CalculationItem": true,
                "VerifiedChecks": [
                        "Mapped to CMA Part 1 Learning Outcome Statements effective September 1, 2024",
                        "Screened to exclude Part 2-only topics such as CVP, financial ratio analysis, capital budgeting, corporate finance, ERM, and ethics",
                        "Original practice item with unique micro-topic and stem",
                        "Answer key distribution balanced across A/B/C/D",
                        "Distractors written as plausible CMA-style traps"
                ],
                "ExplanationWrongA": "",
                "ExplanationWrongB": "A volume variance compares the flexible budget to the static budget — two different activity levels. Here, actual output (8,000 units) equals the flexed budget level, so the volume variance is zero and cannot be $6,000 favorable. The $6,000 difference is also unfavorable (actual costs of $70,000 exceed budgeted costs of $64,000), not favorable.",
                "ExplanationWrongC": "An efficiency variance measures how efficiently inputs were used per unit of output — it compares actual input quantities to standard quantities allowed for actual production. Here, actual output equals budgeted output, so the entire $6,000 difference is a spending (rate) variance: the company paid more per unit of variable cost than the flexible budget anticipated.",
                "ExplanationWrongD": "A $6,000 variance exists because actual costs ($70,000) exceed budgeted costs ($64,000) at the same output level. When actual activity equals flexed budget activity, any cost difference is a spending variance that reflects the difference between the actual cost per unit and the budgeted cost per unit. 'No variance exists' ignores this real $6,000 difference.",
                "question_state": "Certified",
                "DifficultyScore": 3,
                "CognitiveLevel": "Apply"
        }
